statement: A community pool holds $12{,}000$ gallons of water. For repairs, it is drained at a constant rate of $450$ gallons per hour, but at least $3{,}000$ gallons must stay in the pool. What is the greatest number of whole hours the pool can be drained?

choices.misconception: I divided the 3,000 gallons that must stay by 450, about 6.7, and rounded down to 6.
I ignored the 3,000 gallons that must stay and divided 12,000 by 450 to get about 26.7, then rounded down to 26.
I added 3,000 to 12,000 instead of subtracting, and $15{,}000 \div 450 \approx 33.3$, which I rounded down to 33.

hints: How much water is left after $h$ hours of draining?
After $h$ hours the pool holds $12{,}000 - 450h$ gallons. Set this at least 3,000 and solve for $h$.

solutions.reliable: After $h$ hours the pool holds $12{,}000 - 450h$ gallons, and this must be at least $3{,}000$: $12{,}000 - 450h \ge 3{,}000$, so $450h \le 9{,}000$ and $h \le 20$. The greatest whole number of hours is $20$. Check: after $20$ hours exactly $12{,}000 - 9{,}000 = 3{,}000$ gallons remain.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
